other.label: CBO cost estimate: S. 2950, Scam Compound Accountability and Mobilization Act

summary: The Scam Compound Accountability and Mobilization Act requires the U.S. government to create a global strategy and an interagency task force to address international cyber-enabled scam compounds, combat human trafficking and forced criminality associated with them, and hold transnational criminal organizations accountable using financial sanctions and asset forfeiture.

affected_groups.effect: May face U.S. property blocking and transaction prohibitions under presidential sanctions.
affected_groups.group: Foreign persons involved in scam compounds, cyber-enabled fraud, human trafficking, or money laundering

affected_groups.effect: May potentially receive financial redress through future recommendations regarding forfeited assets.
affected_groups.group: U.S. citizen victims of international scam operations

affected_groups.effect: Will receive victim-centered support under the direction of the Ambassador at Large to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons.
affected_groups.group: Survivors of human trafficking and forced criminality

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of State, in consultation with other federal heads, to submit a comprehensive global strategy to counter scam compounds within 180 days.
Establishes an interagency task force within 90 days after the strategy is submitted to coordinate implementation, monitor operations, and report annually for up to six years.

Authorizes the President to impose economic sanctions, including blocking property and transaction prohibitions under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, against foreign persons supporting or operating international scam compounds or enabling services.
Mandates regular semiannual reports to Congress identifying all foreign persons sanctioned under the bill.

Requires the Attorney General to submit a report and assessment within 90 days on existing forfeiture laws, outlining challenges and recommendations for providing financial redress to U.S. citizen victims using forfeited assets.
Sets a sunset date terminating the act seven years after enactment.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budgetary appropriations required to implement the strategy and task force.
Exact criteria for waiver determinations by the President beyond broad national interest.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Scam Compound Accountability and Mobilization Act requires the U.S. government to create a global strategy and an interagency task force to address international cyber-enabled scam compounds, combat human trafficking and forced criminality associated with them, and hold transnational criminal organizations accountable using financial sanctions and asset forfeiture.
summary_detail.significance: The bill directs U.S. foreign policy and executive branch agencies to coordinate international efforts against cyber-enabled fraud and human trafficking compounds, employing targeted sanctions and creating new reporting and victim redress mechanisms over a seven-year period.
